lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set safety stock for all 1,400 SKUs with the economic order quantity (EOQ) formula, balancing ordering and holding costs.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Led the monthly sales and operations planning meeting, reconciling the sales forecast with plant capacity for the finance and production teams.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | May 2019 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Writes the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- Mapped the donation intake process with the warehouse lead and removed two duplicate data-entry steps, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python, SAP
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: The Crestway and food-bank entries present closely matching scope and outcomes, making the achievements look like the same work.
items.because: Their product counts, facility counts, stockout reductions, and inventory savings are so similar that a reader may doubt they are distinct projects.

items.says: Education appears before the recent, directly relevant experience.
items.because: Leading with education delays the work that should anchor an established candidate’s résumé.

items.says: The 11-month gap between the degree and the first listed role is unexplained.
The stockout and inventory results come after the forecasting method.
items.because: That makes the strongest outcome less visible.

items.says: The 15% freight-cost reduction has no stated comparison period or cost basis.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the percentage covers or assess the scale of the savings.

items.says: EOQ does not calculate safety stock; it determines an order quantity.
items.because: Safety stock depends on demand and lead-time uncertainty and a target service level.

items.says: The safety-stock line gives no measured result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the work improved inventory, service levels, or costs.

items.says: The scorecard’s result is buried in a trailing clause.
The line does not say what the delivery-window renegotiations achieved.
The sales-and-operations planning line gives no outcome of reconciling the forecast with plant capacity.
The line does not say what the continued use of the forecasting workflow improved.
The 70%–85% figures do not establish an overall forecast-accuracy gain.
items.because: Excluding SKUs that did not sell every week changes the measured population, so the figures are not a like-for-like measure.

items.says: The bullet uses a first-person possessive.
This is not the strongest opening bullet.
“Writes” is in the wrong tense for a role that ended in January 2021.
The long list of other duties pushes the inventory-accuracy result away from cycle counting.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the strongest outcome after the list.

items.says: The line obscures which work drove the inventory-accuracy gain.
items.because: It is difficult to tell whether cycle counting or another listed responsibility led to the gain.

items.says: The 5% comparison does not say how the deviation was summarized across the delivery logs.
The route pilot is described without saying what it showed.
The line is unclear about what the dispatch team received.
The opening line is too general to show what analysis or recommendations the work involved.
items.because: It does not identify the analysis or tie the recommendations to a specific problem.

items.says: The opening line gives no resulting change or evidence of value from the recommendations.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether they led to a change or what the consulting work achieved.

items.says: The donation-intake improvement should open the entry.
The one-day timing comparison needs a baseline.
The forecast line does not explain its approach.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how the seasonal forecast was built.

items.says: Both outcomes come after the forecast scope.
items.because: A reader has to reach the end of the line to find the stockout and inventory results.

items.says: SAP is listed under Tools, but no experience or project entry shows how it was used.
